findings.title: Pad-energy worksheet stacks four unrooted margins; the pack it implies is about 3x the physics-supported size
findings.evidence: docs/ORDERING.md 8.1.1 and round17_pad_energy.json: board input 5.437970 W = 0.461 A x 5.546 V / 0.8 (3.196 W ports) + 1.4 W logic + 0.825 W continuous SD write + 0.017 W; 2 h at a 6 V charge basis = 1.8127 Ah, 2.2658 Ah after the 20 % reserve. (a) 0.461 A has no stated source anywhere in the repo (grep: only ORDERING 8.1.1, R10_DECISIONS D-R17-01 and the json); REQUIREMENTS Pack row itself gives the ports as about 1.7 W (LR900-F 1 W maker average + GPS 0.05 A, 85 % buck) - the worksheet carries 3.196 W for the same loads. (b) SD write on the pad: F5 logs from launch with a RAM ring buffer, so pad SD power is about 0 W (0.825 W charged for 2 h = 0.275 Ah). (c) 1.4 W logic against REQUIREMENTS Temperature row: firmware runs at 200 MHz; the same row quotes 0.4-1.1 W at 480 MHz, so about 0.17-0.46 W at 200 MHz by dynamic-power scaling (Inference). (d) Wh is converted to Ah at 6 V (2 x 3.0 V, the empty end of the discharge curve), but rated Ah is delivered over the whole curve (about 7.4 V nominal): 10.88 Wh / 7.4 V = 1.47 Ah, not 1.81 Ah. Re-based on the Pack row figures (1.7 W ports + about 0.5 W logic + 0.02 W, 2 h, 7.4 V nominal) the board pad charge is about 0.6 Ah, 0.75 Ah with the 20 % reserve (Inference; arithmetic in the report text). The worksheet text (ORDERING 8.1.1, last paragraph) acknowledges (b) and (c) and keeps the larger numbers "until the owner asks".
findings.impact: The pack is the largest single volume in the main section (about 80 mm battery bay, 50.8 mm bore). A 2.27-5.15 Ah board-only requirement, before motors, flight and recovery are added and divided by 0.8, probably cannot be met inside that bay (pack dimensions not verified here), and it is a margin stack, not a flight need. The two-hour pad wait itself is an owner-stated assumption and is kept.
findings.concrete_fix: Reissue the worksheet on one honest basis: ports from the Pack row (or the maker current of the LR900-F in idle/telemetry mode, cited), SD = 0 W on the pad and 0.825 W only from launch to apogee+30 s, logic from the 200 MHz power in parts_budget.json, Ah = Wh / 7.4 V (or Wh / nominal pack voltage of the chosen cell), and keep the single 0.8 usable-capacity factor. Records only, no board change.

findings.title: The inherited switch-bounce network delays recovery after a real power loss to 0.4-1.1 s, against the owner failsafe of a neutral command within 50 ms
findings.evidence: docs/REQUIREMENTS.md F6 and Accepted risks: reboot after a brownout longer than the ride-through "about 1.1 s"; battery_entry.kicad_sch note on C87: (R80+R165)||R81 = 227 kohm charges C87 2.2 uF, so turn-on takes 0.4-1.1 s, and bounce shorter than 0.11/0.21/0.27 s at 6.0/7.4/8.4 V cannot trip U9. R10_DECISIONS "Owner questions closed by physics" (GAP list): "neutral quickly" = neutral PWM within 50 ms; F6 Reset/startup allocation <= 48.653 ms. REQUIREMENTS Flight table: stuck-tab roll estimate about 1100 deg/s. Board: C87 is 2.2 uF 16 V X5R (C23630, shared code with C19/C20), R81 300 kohm. R18-REQ-12 added a bench acceptance of "longest contact drop-out < 10 ms", which a time constant of about 0.1 uF x 300 kohm = 30 ms already covers.
findings.impact: The owner failsafe (tab back to neutral quickly after reset/hang/brownout) is met by the IWDG path but not after a supply interruption longer than about 0.2 s (loose screw, a real battery break): U9 turns off, and recovery waits 0.4-1.1 s for C87 to recharge before boot even starts. That is about the time a stuck tab needs to spin the vehicle up. The 0.15 s immunity it buys has no measured root (R18-REQ-12) and the proposed acceptance (10 ms) needs one tenth of it.
findings.concrete_fix: Owner/bench decision, not a fix-now: after the contact-chatter measurement, set C87 from the measured longest drop-out (physics supports about 0.1-0.22 uF: R81 x C87 = 30-66 ms discharge and a 0.02-0.1 s turn-on). C14663 100 nF 0603 is already a stocked code, so the 2.2 uF line drops from 3 to 2 parts and no code is added. Update F6 and the Accepted-risks 1.1 s line to match. Keep the board as it is until the measurement exists.

findings.title: docs/M3_ACTUATOR_MERGE.md is cited as a current source but describes removed hardware and has no superseded banner
findings.evidence: AGENTS.md section 1 table rows "Actuator power switch" and "Shorted-igniter current limit" cite docs/M3_ACTUATOR_MERGE.md (and section 2.6); REQUIREMENTS F7 and F8 cite it. The file (status "design + CAD only", 2026-09-25 R2) describes: two independent pyro channels each with its own fused bus; Q120/Q121 AON6403 C2760089 (board has AONR21357 C431196); 7.7 A actuator rail with servo header; R122/R123 100k/100k from RAW_PROTECTED (board: R122 1 kohm from PC1, R123 2 kohm); C121 470 uF on RAW_ACT (absent); RAW_ACT sense R124/R125 to PB0 (absent); in-line 15 A fuse; launch pull-pin (J123, removed); the ARM terminal (J124, removed). Only section 2.6 survives. The first line has no banner (head -25 read).
findings.impact: AGENTS section 1 sends reviewers to it for the Q120/Q121 and R134 design; a reader who follows the link meets the opposite of the single-switch, off-board-servo design (for example, "the actuator rail is on only when the U9 logic path is on", "servo header").
findings.concrete_fix: Add a one-line banner at the top: "Historical R2 record. Current for R10: section 2.6 (shorted-igniter limit) only; everything else is superseded by R10_DECISIONS single-switch, AUD-3/4/6 and D-R18-01/02." In AGENTS rows, cite "M3_ACTUATOR_MERGE.md section 2.6" only for the R134 limit and point the Q120/Q121 row to M3_R10.md "Power". Text only.

findings.title: P3 keeps a 500 g-equivalent (5 x 100 g) retention load with a basis that names no flight number for it
findings.evidence: docs/REQUIREMENTS.md P3 (post-fix text): 100 g design load is "close to the 92 g landing case of DESIGN_ASSURANCE 6.1"; boost loads 28-37 g (flight table); "the parent VEHICLE.md gives no ejection g figure, so the 500 g equivalent stays until it is measured or replaced by the owner". Retention is open, "not passed by inspection".
findings.impact: The fix pass only recorded the basis; the 5x factor over the largest stated load (about 2.7x the 37 g peak is already in the 100 g) remains a margin that every release carries as open and that drives staking and standoff rework.
findings.concrete_fix: Owner choice: restate P3 as 100 g design load with a retention factor of 2 (200 g equivalent) for C84, DB125 bodies, J3 shell and LS120, or give the ejection/shock-cord snatch figure that needs more. Text and first-article pull/mass test only.

findings.title: C84 hold-up (470 uF, hand-fitted) has no derived required duration, and its 0.49-0.57 ms ports-on figure is shorter than the actions the text names
findings.evidence: REQUIREMENTS F6: hold-up to 3.8 V at 300.8 uF is 0.490-0.571 ms with all ports and the card writing (1.533-1.655 ms camera off/logic shed); OQ-5 in R10_DECISIONS: "do whatever AVA does", no hold-up time derived. No document states the time the logic must stay alive. Winbond W25Q128JV tPP (page program) 0.4 ms typical, 3 ms maximum (datasheet AC table, cached copy line "Page Program Time tPP 0.4 3 ms"); TPS2553 turn-off up to 3 ms (R10_DECISIONS Always-on ports, same text). F6 itself forbids a blocking flush on sag. The cost: C84 is an 8 x 10 mm polymer part with no maker reflow profile, so it is excluded from the JLC upload and hand-fitted after both reflows (D-R18-09), plus a C84 staking and retention item in P3.
findings.impact: With no stated need, the 470 uF cannot be judged oversized or adequate. It is too short to finish one QSPI page program (3 ms) with the ports on, and the only action that fits (PA6 analog watchdog interrupt, stop writes, lower camera OE: tens of microseconds to under 0.2 ms) needs far less than 470 uF. The part costs a manual assembly step, a height/ESR first-article check and a retention item.
findings.concrete_fix: Record the hold-up requirement as a time: the interval the firmware needs after the PA6 watchdog fires (measure on the bench: ADC watchdog latency + shed sequence). If it is about 0.2 ms, 100-220 uF satisfies it and the capacitor can be a reflow-rated part with a maker profile; if the intent is one QSPI page (3 ms), 470 uF is not enough with the ports on and the text should say so. Owner decision (OQ-5 is an owner mandate); no board change now.

rejected_or_closed_candidates.candidate: Q120/Q121 back-to-back pair is redundant now that servo power is off the board
rejected_or_closed_candidates.reason: Q121 (drain RAW_ACT, source common) is the forward-blocking FET; Q120 (drain BAT_IN) blocks reverse. Without Q120 a reversed pack would drive RAW_ACT negative through the Q121 body diode and put about -0.7 V on the ARM1_SENSE divider (PC5 injection). The pair is rooted in the accepted reverse-pack case and costs one 3 x 3 mm part; closed.

rejected_or_closed_candidates.candidate: U401 4.8 V LDO after the 5.3 V buck is an unnecessary stage
rejected_or_closed_candidates.reason: D-R1-03: camera needs at least 5 V, the radio maker specifies 4.5-5 V, one adjustable rail cannot guarantee both; physical root.

rejected_or_closed_candidates.candidate: Camera U12/U13/U402 isolation vs direct GPS/radio UARTs
rejected_or_closed_candidates.reason: The camera is the only switched supply (camera off on the pad, D-CIR-02); a powered MCU pin through 1 kohm into an unpowered camera is a state GPS/radio never have. Owner condition in the always-on-ports decision satisfied.
Rooted in FMEA I-9: a single shorted top puts hundreds of mA-class current into the igniter path or the MCU pin; tolerance of one shorted/open part is the stated requirement.

OVLO 1.20 V +/-1.9 % and ILIM +/-10 % for ILIM > 1 A (TPS25947 datasheet p.1 and electrical table) dominate; OV threshold 9.77 V typical, 9.5-10.1 V with 1 % resistors, still above 8.7 V (LiHV) and below 12.6 V. Cost is under $0.2 per board and no space or routing effect; not worth a finding. R400-R403 (buck feedback, 5.03 V camera minimum) are justified.
